text:
Alice: AcmeCorp. Streaming sessions started getting intermittent 504s around 09:10 UTC. Customer sees SDK stuck in retry loop, lots of reconnects. Sample request ids: rq_8f3a, rq_8f3b. p95 latency up and ~15% 504s on /v1/stream endpoint.
Ben: Pulling gateway logs for those request ids now. I’m seeing a pattern: a flurry of auth-service lookups returning 404/401 for the same token, then upstream reset: 'RST_STREAM'. Looks like token churn + stream window reset.
Carol: Customer reported they upgraded an internal token-rotation client yesterday — it had a bug that retries token fetch every 500ms on failure. Could cause auth QPS spike.
Support-bot: Incident INC-4121 created and linked to this thread. Priority: high.
Dave: Reprobed locally with a small script to mimic token-refresh fanout + streaming open. Command: ```for i in {1..200}; do curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream & done``` Within 30s I see many connections receiving 504 and occasional RST_STREAM.
Ben: Gateway metrics show auth service requests per-tenant spiked 40x for acmecorp. Edge proxy has concurrent-streams limit kicking in which produces 504s when upstream closes.
Ben: Also noticing the SDK retry behavior: backoff not exponential in their older SDK version — ends up flooding with short retries.
Carol: Customer says they can push a hotfix to their SDK to implement exponential backoff and avoid rotating tokens on 401. They've already rolled a client patch to stop retries on token-fetch failures.
Alice: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Rate-limit token validation QPS per tenant at the gateway 2) Bump concurrent-streams for edge pool for 30m 3) Ask customer to pause aggressive refreshes. Which do we want now?
Erin: I drafted a customer comms message: apology + ask to apply client patch (we'll provide recommended backoff config) + temporary guidance to use long-lived token until patch rolls out. Customer OK with that.
Ben: Ops suggestion: increase max_concurrent_streams on edge-proxies for that pool and add a fast-fail for obviously invalid tokens to reduce auth-service fanout. I can apply the config to one region as a canary.
Deploy-bot: Rollout started: edge-proxies-config-v2 to eu-west-1 (1/4).
Dave: Applied edge config canary in eu-west-1. Observed auth QPS down ~60% for that tenant after fast-fail introduced. 504s dropped to ~2% in that region.
Ben: Corroborating logs: auth cache hit-rate improved after fast-fail and edge config bump. SDK backoff change from customer reduced retry flood.
Alice: Customer update sent: asked them to keep the client patch and advised short-term token reuse. They replied: "we rolled the patch and saw immediate improvement".
Erin: Customer metrics show stabilized p95 and 504s now under 1%. They thanked us for quick response and said they'll ship the SDK fix to all customers.
Alice: Next steps: - Postmortem with timeline (assign to Ben/Carol) - Add per-tenant token-refresh telemetry + alert when refresh rate > 10/min - Update SDK guidance page with recommended backoff config and token rotation patterns.
Support-bot: Incident INC-4121 status: mitigated.
Alice: Closing this thread after postmortem created.
